author: @mel
text:
Where is the Euro going....?

The market's action these past weeks might have felt a little odd to
lots of traders including myself but I took the time to make a detailed
analysis on the Euro wich is my favorite pair as you might know by now.
 :)

The Euro can act like a charm when it trades in a clear direction but a
few times per year it can act really "strangly" and fool lots of
traders. However all this can be explained imo.

The chart below is a monthly chart. The blue line on it is a significant
 level , it acted as as s/d and last action there was a bull action.
This line is now demand and last month candle closed above it.

Following chart is the Weekly chart, On this chart you'll see the
Monthly demand aswell (thin blue line) but if we look at this TF, we see
 the lower black line wich is a clear demand too.

So, to resume everything so far , we have had a reaction of Monthly
Demand , price then traded , we also have a weekly close (last week's
candle) that closed below another weekly demand wich now turned Supply.

So far I'm thinking that a revisit of Demand might therefore be an option.

Next chart is the Daily one, I added an upper blue dahed line wich is
Supply aswell as a pink dashed line wich is a previous supply that
turned demand yesterday.

Yesterday's candle closed above the demand and it closes of it's low
wich show some buying, however it didn't closed above the demand at the
dashed blue line yet. It cloed right beneath a 4h supply level So if it
 didn't broke the supply, we might see a pullback from here.

Following chart is a 4h chart.

All the previous line from Monthly to daily are still on this chart, I
added other blue lines wich show some potential recation points. As you
can see the upper blue line is the supply that stoped price yesterday.

We also have an engulf of the middle blue line (demand).

So.... I definately see some bullish signs coming in and explained why
above. However, if price breaks the HTF's demand I talked about, this
would definately be over.

I would prefer to wait for a nice pullback to long for longs, preferably
 to the source of the demand. However, this might not the safest way to
trade the Euro right now.

You remember when I said above that the market were acting odd and that all this could be explained?

Well, below's chart is again a 4h chart , I removed the blue lines from the last charts so that you can see the clear picture.

To me this looks like some accumulation and the fact that price arrived
at a Higher Timeframe demand, in this case Monthly, might explain why
price was acting so "odd".

On this timeframe price is clearly in a range and the safest way to trade this is to wait for a clear break and than a pullback.

So if the bulls want to take this higher, the upper blue dashed line would have to be broken with a clear close above it.

So let's see what price will do, I would prefer longs as there is lots
of place for price to move but unfortunatley I can't decide about it and
 will have to react to what PA tells me

Best,

Mel
